Asha (Sec): Announcement: new privileged access policy effective 2026-06-01. We are rolling out Just-In-Time (JIT) admin access and mandatory session recording for interactive privileged sessions (bastion, DB admin, K8s kubectl, cloud consoles). This reduces standing privileges and improves auditability. Read below and act.
Omar (SecOps): Scope: interactive admin access across prod and infra projects. Non-interactive service-to-service tokens not affected. We will apply JIT and recording to SSH bastions, RDP jump hosts, k8s-admin roles, and DB admin consoles.
Priya (DevEx): Runbook and checklist link: https://redwood.internal/docs/security/jit-session-recording. TL;DR: 1) onboard systems to the JIT gateway (or use our proxy agent), 2) remove users from permanent admin groups, 3) configure session recording retention and access controls, 4) test playback and audit queries.
Raj (DevTools): How will humans request access? Do we have CLI/Slack flow?
Omar (SecOps): Access request flows: - CLI: `redwood-jit request --role k8s-admin --ttl 2h --reason "hotfix"` - Slack app: /request-access which opens approval dialog to on-call. Approval options: auto-approve for owners, manual approve for others. All requests require justification and scoped TTL.
Asha (Sec): Recording retention: 90 days by default; 1 year available for compliance teams via request. Access to recordings is RBAC-protected and audited. Sensitive session redaction: recording system will mask OTPs and known secrets patterns; however teams should avoid exposing secrets in sessions.
infra-oncall: What about emergency access during incidents when approvals are slow?
Omar (SecOps): Emergency flow: infra-oncall can grant a 30-minute emergency token with post-hoc justification. recorder-bot will tag these sessions and require a follow-up incident entry. Abuse will result in review.
recorder-bot: Note: playback and transcription available. Transcripts are searchable but classified; only approved roles can query transcripts. Integrations: SIEM will ingest session metadata and alerts for suspicious commands.
Priya (DevEx): Migration helpers? I can add JIT client and a pre-check to quickstart templates so new services are configured against the gateway. Suggest a small `redwood-jit` wrapper that prints required env vars and validates playback after granting access.
Asha (Sec): Action items: 1) owners of privileged systems must integrate with JIT gateway by 2026-05-15. 2) remove users from standing admin groups and ensure workflows use JIT requests by 2026-06-01. 3) run playback test and paste results into ticket SEC-5301. 4) if you need a longer TTL for a justified workflow, request an exception in SEC-5301 with mitigation.
Raj (DevTools): Will this break automation that currently SSH-es with admin keys?
Omar (SecOps): Yes, automate should use service accounts and short-lived machine credentials; any automation using human credentials must be migrated. We will run a scan for interactive sessions initiated by non-service accounts and list offenders.
sec-bot: Automated audit scheduled: weekly privileged-group membership snapshot + session coverage report. Initial scan shows ~120 users in standing admin groups and ~45 hosts missing the recording agent. Results posted to SEC-5301.
Priya (DevEx): ETA for CLI helper and templates: initial PR by EOW, follow-ups next sprint.
infra-oncall: I'll coordinate a phased rollout: infra projects first week, then product teams the next two weeks, with migration office hours. Will create calendar invites.
Asha (Sec): Noncompliance after 2026-06-01 will result in temporary access revocation for standing groups and mandatory review. Join office hours Thurs 9am PT or ping sec-oncall. :lock: :mag:
